summary: The root حيف (Hyf) signifies acting wrongfully, unjustly, or tyrannically, especially in judgment. It implies inclining to wrong or deviating from right.
lane: 1 حَافَ حاف حافي , aor. يَحِيفُ , (S, Msb,) inf. n. حَيْفٌ , (S, Msb, K,) He (a judge, or any other person, Msb) acted wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically, (S, Msb, K,) عَلَيْهِ against him: (S:) or, as some say, he inclined [ to that which was wrong ], or declined [ from that which was right ], in his judgment. (TA.) حَيْفُ النَّاحِلِ means A man's giving to certain of his children exclusively of others: he should treat them equally, and not prefer some before others. (T, TA.)

headwords.gloss: Acting wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously; tyrannically; declining from the right direction

parts.t: (Lth, Msb, K: [in some copies of the K,
who does not attain the object of his want.

headwords.def: حَائِفٌ Acting wrongfully, unjustly, injuriously, or tyrannically: (Lth, Msb, K: [in some copies of the K, حَائِرٌ is erroneously put for جَائِرٌ :] pl. حَافَةٌ (Msb, K) and حُيَّفٌ (K, Msb *) and حُيُفٌ . (TA.) An arrow declining from the right direction. (TA.) And, as being likened thereto, (tropical:) An impotent man, who does not attain the object of his want. (TA.) The side of a mountain. (K, TA.) headwords.gloss: A district; the like; a land, upon which rain has not fallen
